tasks.title: Library Study Room Bookings
tasks.prompt:
A library has 3 study rooms. Bookings are given as room number, start minute, end minute (minutes since midnight). Rooms cannot have overlapping bookings.

Bookings:
Booking 1: room 1, start 540, end 600
Booking 2: room 1, start 620, end 700
Booking 3: room 2, start 540, end 660
Booking 4: room 2, start 680, end 780
Booking 5: room 3, start 550, end 640
Booking 6: room 3, start 650, end 720
Booking 7: room 1, start 720, end 800
Booking 8: room 2, start 800, end 900

Write a program that for each room prints the total booked minutes and the longest gap (idle minutes) between consecutive bookings within that room's first and last booking times, then prints the overall total booked minutes across all rooms.

Output exactly 4 lines:

Room 1: BBB min booked, GGG min longest gap
Room 2: BBB min booked, GGG min longest gap
Room 3: BBB min booked, GGG min longest gap
TOTAL BOOKED: TTTT min

Where BBB is 3-digit zero-padded booked minutes for that room, GGG is 3-digit zero-padded longest gap between consecutive bookings (gap = next_start - prev_end; if only one booking, gap is 000), and TTTT is 4-digit zero-padded sum across all rooms.

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Room 1: 220 min booked, 020 min longest gap
Room 2: 320 min booked, 020 min longest gap
Room 3: 160 min booked, 010 min longest gap
TOTAL BOOKED: 0700 min
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

tasks.title: Orchard Irrigation Scheduling
tasks.prompt:
An orchard has 5 irrigation zones. Each zone needs watering for a specified number of minutes per day, and the watering system can only run one zone at a time. Zones must be watered in order 1 through 5, starting at minute 360 (6:00 AM).

Zone watering durations (minutes): Zone 1: 45, Zone 2: 60, Zone 3: 30, Zone 4: 75, Zone 5: 50.

After each zone, there is a 10-minute system flush before the next zone can start (no flush needed after the last zone).

Write a program that prints, for each zone, its start minute, end minute, and duration; then prints the total time from first start to last end, and the total water-on time (sum of zone durations).

Output exactly 7 lines:

Zone 1: SSS-EEE (DDD min)
Zone 2: SSS-EEE (DDD min)
Zone 3: SSS-EEE (DDD min)
Zone 4: SSS-EEE (DDD min)
Zone 5: SSS-EEE (DDD min)
TOTAL SPAN: TTT min
WATER ON: WWW min

Where SSS and EEE are 3-digit zero-padded start and end minutes, DDD is 3-digit zero-padded duration, TTT is 3-digit zero-padded total span from minute 360 to the last zone's end, and WWW is 3-digit zero-padded sum of all zone durations.

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Zone 1: 360-405 (045 min)
Zone 2: 415-475 (060 min)
Zone 3: 485-515 (030 min)
Zone 4: 525-600 (075 min)
Zone 5: 610-660 (050 min)
TOTAL SPAN: 300 min
WATER ON: 260 min
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

tasks.title: Train Network Departures

    {"name": "Red", "stops": [{"station": "Central", "minutes": 0}, {"station": "Market", "minutes": 4}, {"station": "Harbor", "minutes": 9}]},

Lines: 3
Red stops: 3
Blue stops: 2
Green stops: 2
Red fare: 2.50
Blue fare: 3.75

    {"label": "W1", "x": 5, "y": 3},
    {"label": "W2", "x": 5, "y": 7},

  ],
  "obstacles": [{"x": 3, "y": 5}, {"x": 4, "y": 6}],

W4: (1,4)

tasks.title: Aquarium Sensor Readings
tasks.prompt:
You are given the following JSON text describing aquarium sensors:

{
  "tanks": [
    {"name": "Fresh", "ph": 7.1, "temp_c": 24.5, "fish": 12},
    {"name": "Salt", "ph": 8.2, "temp_c": 26.0, "fish": 8},
    {"name": "Brack", "ph": 7.8, "temp_c": 25.3, "fish": 5},
    {"name": "Quarantine", "ph": 7.0, "temp_c": 23.9, "fish": 2}
  ],
  "ph_min": 7.0,
  "ph_max": 8.0,
  "temp_target": 25.0
}

Write a program that parses this JSON and prints exactly the following lines (no trailing spaces):

Tanks: 4
In range: Fresh, Brack, Quarantine
Out of range: Salt
Total fish: 27
Avg ph: 7.53
Warmest: Salt
Needs heating: Fresh, Quarantine, Brack
Avg temp: 24.93

Notes:
- A tank's ph is "in range" if ph_min <= ph <= ph_max.
- "Total fish" is the sum of fish across all tanks.
- "Avg ph" is the arithmetic mean of all ph values.
- "Warmest" is the name of the tank with the highest temp_c (break ties by first appearance).
- "Needs heating" lists tanks whose temp_c is strictly less than temp_target, in order of appearance, separated by ", ".
- "Avg temp" is the arithmetic mean of all temp_c values.
- Real numbers must be printed with exactly 2 decimal places.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Tanks: 4
In range: Fresh, Brack, Quarantine
Out of range: Salt
Total fish: 27
Avg ph: 7.52
Warmest: Salt
Needs heating: Fresh, Quarantine
Avg temp: 24.93

tasks.title: Bakery Recipe Key Paths
tasks.prompt:
A bakery stores its recipe configuration as a nested JSON document. You must walk the document and print every key path and its value, one per line, in depth-first order (parent before children, children in the order they appear).

The JSON document is:
{
  "recipe": {
    "name": "Sourdough",
    "flour": {"type": "Rye", "grams": 500},
    "water": {"ml": 350, "tempC": 22},
    "salt": {"grams": 10, "added": true}
  }
}

Print one line per scalar (non-object) value found. The line format is:
<full dot-separated key path> = <value>

For example, the first line would be recipe.name = Sourdough.

Rules:
- Booleans print as true or false.
- Integers print as plain integers with no decimal point.
- Real numbers print with exactly 1 decimal place.
- Objects themselves are not printed; only their leaf values are.
- There are no trailing spaces on any line.

Output exactly these 7 lines in this order:
recipe.name = Sourdough
recipe.flour.type = Rye
recipe.flour.grams = 500
recipe.water.ml = 350
recipe.water.tempC = 22.0
recipe.salt.grams = 10
recipe.salt.added = true
tasks.expected_stdout:
recipe.name = Sourdough
recipe.flour.type = Rye
recipe.flour.grams = 500
recipe.water.ml = 350
recipe.water.tempC = 22
recipe.salt.grams = 10
recipe.salt.added = true
tasks.category: converting between a JSON document and formatted text output (tables, key paths, type checks of mixed values)

Build an inverted index from each target word "knight", "card", and "die" to the list of line numbers (1-based, ascending) whose text contains that word.

knight: 1 3 6 8
card: 5 7
die: 4 9
